note: The review desk gained a read-only Triage tab: the 'what needs you' view over the served store's decisions -- ranked open decisions, near-duplicate clusters, and proposed supersedes/contradicts edges -- reusing the existing nestor.triage engine (which seals nothing by construction) and the graph view's _decision_domains so the two never disagree about what a decision is. Built by a sub-agent in an isolated worktree, then audited: the write-refusal test was confirmed substantive (it seeds an edge-producing store, forges status/verifier/seal_sig/edge fields, and asserts the store is byte-for-byte unchanged), and the endpoint confirmed GET-only. Driving it for real against the 380-decision dogfood store then caught what the agent's small-store tests could not: /api/triage took ~23s with no loading affordance, reading as a frozen tab. Fixed here before merge.

decisions.question: Should decision triage (clustering, proposed supersedes/contradicts edges, the ranked open list) be surfaced at the nestor ui review desk, and should the first cut be read-only?
decisions.commitment: Yes -- add GET /api/triage (built from nestor.triage.triage() over the served store's own decision-domain pairs via _decision_domains, shared with the Graph tab) and a Triage tab that renders it. Read-only: there is no POST /api/triage, no write path, and the view seals nothing. Confirming or rejecting a proposed edge is deliberately out of scope for this pass -- it is a human-authority write and is the next bite.
decisions.why: The triage intelligence already existed in nestor/triage/ but was reachable only through an offline CLI over the dogfood decision files -- invisible to whoever is actually sealing against a live store at the desk (the §6.107 gap: the UI was built for an operator who read the docstrings). Read-only-first keeps the propose/confirm line intact while answering 'what needs my attention' before any edge-confirmation ceremony is built. The ordering is derived from the Report's own structure (a contradiction or a multi-member cluster ahead of a singleton), not a new invented score.
decisions.doors_closed: No edge-write or confirm/reject affordance on this screen -- that needs its own POST endpoint behind the existing seal/verifier authority, deliberately unbuilt here. No re-implementation of triage: the built organ is reused unmodified.

decisions.question: Triage clustering is O(n^2) in the decision count and took ~23s over the 380-decision store, freezing the tab with no feedback. How is that made acceptable without changing the propose-not-confirm covenant or the matcher?
decisions.commitment: Memoize the /api/triage response on the App under a sha256 signature of the decisions (id, status, question, commitment): computed once per store-state, reused until a seal, edit, or new decision changes the signature (measured: first call ~22s, second ~0.007s). Paint a 'computing...' loading card before the first uncached compute so the tab reads as working, not broken. Both are read-only -- the cache holds only a response dict, guarded by a module lock while the compute runs outside it.
decisions.why: A 23s frozen tab is the opposite of the human-facing goal this view exists for, and the slowness is the StringMatcher being the binding constraint (IDEAS §3.4/§6.106), not a fixable algorithm here. Caching is honest because triage is a pure function of the decisions -- the signature invalidates it the moment the store changes, so a human never sees a triage that no longer matches what they are sealing against (pinned by a test that a new decision recomputes). Doors closed: a blunt compute-once-forever cache (would serve stale triage after a seal); loosening the matcher or the bar to go faster (would change what the view says, not just how fast it says it).
